artifacts.summary: Confirms all reported root causes at the line level, live-reproduces all false positives (including a new race-condition finding for the self-subshell case) on this machine read-only, and recommends a unifying single-snapshot ps -eo comm/cgroup/uid/liveness redesign plus a sourceable-main() test design closing all four required regression assertions.

memory_candidates.content: ps -eo pid,ppid,uid,tty,etimes,rss,comm,cgroup,args --no-headers is a single atomic snapshot (procps-ng, verified on NixOS) that supplies executable identity (comm), cgroup path, and owning UID in one call -- use this instead of a two-stage 'ps aux | grep <argv substring>' plus a later re-query for ancestor/tree-membership checks. A later, second live re-query against PIDs captured in an earlier snapshot risks a race: transient/short-lived candidate PIDs (e.g. a script's own subshells) may have already exited by the time the second query runs, causing ancestor-walk-style checks to silently fail closed to 'not excluded' (unsafe fail-open) rather than correctly recognizing membership.

For bash scripts that need both CLI-executable and test-sourceable behavior, guard a main() call with `if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then main "$@"; fi`. This lets a regression suite `source` the script to unit-test individual predicate/helper functions directly, without spawning subprocesses for every case, while keeping normal execution completely unchanged. This is a standard bash idiom, not a test-only instrumentation hack, and is consistent with the shell-testing convention that scripts under test should never be modified to 'know' they are being tested.
